key_insight: LesionAgent combines an LLM with frozen 3D imaging tools and a structured verification harness to track tumors and assess treatment response without task-specific training.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest that tool orchestration, persistent lesion memory, and deterministic clinical rules can matter more than the choice of LLM for reliable imaging workflows.
method: Operates frozen 3D detection, segmentation, registration, and tracking models through coordinate-labelled views.
Maintains a longitudinal lesion registry and verifies model outputs before relying on them.
Delegates numerical response assessment to a deterministic clinical-guideline engine.
evidence_signal: Across four public longitudinal CT datasets, it outperformed automatic baselines in tracking and measurement; false progression calls fell from 33/56 with fixed-rule chaining to 2/56, and clinical response agreement reached 20/23 follow-ups.
watch_item: Clinical response evaluation covered only 23 follow-ups; broader prospective validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
